examined.reason: The grid kernel now computes row-local shared offsets and allocates (depth+1)*width words per group. Reviewed the actual instruction lists, address bounds, per-group producer identity, universal output and VJP contracts, and finite admitted execution construction. Numerical hypotheses and the independent single-group implementation are unchanged.

Dense launches use the compact kernel in the same grid semantics. Shared location identity still includes the group; candidate reads, graph admission, barriers, schedules and pointwise stages are unchanged.

The check now audits 53 additional public compact-kernel declarations and builds six added modules, preserving exact endpoint matching, pinned dependencies, source guards and the distinction from hardware conformance.

The example still provides the same dense-ReLU computation, generated backward correspondence, explicit numerical conditions and reproducible evidence. The improved internal allocation does not change this parent responsibility.

No instruction, memory, barrier, arithmetic result relation, or scheduling rule changed. The compact program uses the same operations, now computing local shared offsets in registers; the instruction-level existence and universal correctness proofs check this implementation.
